nce | 50 |

Every order line has a `line/sku` ref to its hub.

**Crosswalk (hubs carrying each system's ID, by tier)**
- **Shopify, 49 of 49 hubs:**
  - 34 are exact, 15 normalized (0.9).
  - The normalized ones had a lowercase code, a missing zero-pad (`AH-CTB-16-LRG`) or a compacted code (`AHUTN0017NAT`).
- **3PL, 49 of 49 hubs:**
  - Exact, because the UPC barcode is the same in Shopify and the 3PL.
  - The 3PL's own client SKU is blank for 5 items, and wrong for 5 more by one adjacent-letter swap (BKL, WTH, SVL, HFL, BMA). Matching on UPC sidesteps both.
- **Amazon, 25 of 49 hubs:** ASIN, FNSKU and seller SKU.
  - Exact where the spelling is the same, normalized (0.9) where Amazon adds a `-FBA` suffix.
  - The other 24 hubs have no Amazon listing in the export, so they are unmatched.
- **Factory item code, supplier and HS code, 49 of 49 hubs:**
  - Corroborated (0.7). The commercial invoices carry no shared code, but the factory's item description equals Shopify's product title plus variant, one to one.
- **Suppliers to QuickBooks vendors, 8 of 8:**
  - Normalized (0.9), matched by the vendor email domain (`@nbbw.example` is supplier `NBBW`).
  - The 3 service vendors have no supplier code and are indexed by name only.
- **Hub code spelling:** I used the well-formed spelling (`AH-FAM-NNNN-CCC`), which Shopify and Amazon use for the colour codes.

**Attributes registered (13)**
- **Shopify identifiers:** `shopify/order_id`, `shopify/order_name`, `shopify/customer_id` and `shopify/line_item_id`. `order_name` is the key the 3PL quotes.
- **Amazon identifiers:** `amazon/order_id`, `amazon/order_line_key` and `amazon/inbound_shipment_id`.
- **3PL and QuickBooks identifiers:** `tpl/receipt_no`, `tpl/receipt_line_key` and `quickbooks/vendor_name`.
- **Join keys:** `order/customer`, `line/sku` and `receipt/po`.
- **Why `distinct_from`:** I registered `line/sku` against `po_line/sku`, which is for purchase order lines. The other near matches were only attributes in the same batch.
- **Why composite keys:** Amazon's export gives no line ID, so `amazon/order_line_key` is the order ID plus the listed SKU. The 3PL's `tpl/receipt_line_key` is the receipt number plus the item code.

I recorded which system is authoritative for each identifier: shopify, amazon, 3pl and quickbooks.

**Duplicate customers:** 154 accounts are marked `core/same_as` the oldest account in their group. There are 148 pairs and 3 trios.
- 84 match on the same mailbox once normalized (0.9).
- 70 match only on the same full name and postal address, with different emails (0.7).

**Terms the sources disagree on**
- **SKU spelling:** Shopify, Amazon and the 3PL each spell our SKU differently, as described above. I kept each system's own IDs and wrote one hub code.
- **Inventory quantity:** the sources count stock differently. The 3PL has on hand, allocated, available and damaged; Amazon has fulfillable, unsellable and reserved; Shopify has one `inventoryQuantity`. None is indexed, since quantities stay in their source.

**For a human to decide**
- **Name-plus-address duplicates:** please review the 70 at 0.7, in case two people share a name and address.
- **Outbound shipments not indexed:** the 3PL's 37,332 outbound rows have no ID of their own. They name a Shopify order or an FBA inbound shipment ID; 187 rows are FBA transfers.
- **Receipts not linked to shipments:** 33 receipt rows have a blank PO reference. The "Container #" column sometimes holds a house bill of lading number, so I did not link receipts to shipments.
- **Stub POs:** `receipt/po` created 19 `po/number` entities. They are stubs for the ingestion skill to fill.
- **Left out:** Shopify product (parent) IDs, Amazon buyer data (none in the export), the QuickBooks general ledger (rule 4 forbids it), and the PDFs and chats beyond the item, HS-code and supplier crosswalk. I also did not index the purchase orders, shipments, inspections and customs entries in the documents; that is the ingestion skill's job.

ingest.final:
ngested the supplier PDFs, the chats and the inbox, except the 41 commercial invoice/packing list PDFs, which I skipped as already read (below). The store now holds the new facts, each transaction pointing at its source document with a confidence. My dry run found no unresolved items, and the counts after the real run look right: 32 shipments, 31 of them with both booking and house bill numbers.

## Documents
| Kind | Read |
|---|---|
| Proforma invoices | 48 |
| Inspection reports | 46 |
| Chat messages with facts | 62, from 8 chats (the other messages carry none) |
| Forwarder emails | 32 booking confirmations, 4 rolled bookings, 31 pre-alerts, 7 ETA updates and 30 arrival notices |
| Warehouse emails | 29 receipt-complete |
| Customs broker emails | 30 entry summaries |
| Skipped as already read | 41 commercial invoices and packing lists |

## What was written
- **Purchase orders:** 48 with PI number, supplier, ETD and currency, and 196 PO lines.
- **Suppliers:** 8 updated with the letterhead name, Chinese name, address, incoterm and payment terms. I took the letterhead name as supplier/name because that attribute was empty.
- **Inspections:** 46.
- **Shipments:** 32, with 166 shipment lines.
- **Customs entries:** 30.
- **PO status after the run:** 37 received, 4 shipped, 3 in production, 3 confirmed and 1 ready.
- **Shipment status after the run:** 29 delivered, 1 arrived, 1 departed and 1 booked.

## Confidence below 1 (62 facts)
- **ETD changes from chats (18):**
  - The dates are written without a year, so I read each as the next occurrence after the message, in China time. Message times were converted from New York time.
  - Confidence is 0.9 when the message names the PO. It is 0.8 when it names the PI number only.
  - The 48 "ETD …" messages sent with each PI matched the PI's printed date, so I wrote nothing for them.
- **Container numbers from chats (15):** 0.8. No PO is named, so I found the shipment by container number, supplier and loading date, because containers are reused across voyages.
- **Production started (25 deposit acknowledgements, 6 "大货生产中" messages):** the deposit acknowledgements are 0.9 when the PO is named and 0.8 when I took the PO from the PI sent just before. The "大货生产中" messages name no PO, so I used the chat's latest PI at 0.6.

## Needs your attention
- **The 41 commercial invoices and packing lists were skipped by rule 8.** The catalogue run cited them as evidence for SKU facts, but they produced no shipment facts. The pre-alert emails carry the same lines, cartons and containers, so little is lost. Origin and destination come from the bookings. Tell me if you want them re-read.
- **Duplicate PO entities in the catalogue:** 12 catalogue POs carry combined numbers such as "PO-2025-0149 / PO-2025-0145 / PO-2025-0150", and the 3PL receipts point at them. I created separate POs under the exact numbers and left the combined ones alone. Someone should split or merge them.
- **Hash conventions:** for emails I hashed the raw message from its `From ` line with the blank separator line removed. For chat messages I hashed the header and text lines without a trailing newline. A different convention would make these hashes mismatch.

## Not recorded (no attribute for them)
- **Warehouse discrepancies (21 emails):** damaged counts almost everywhere, and two short receipts. One is 24 short on AH-BWL-0015-CLY, expected 1680 and received 1656, on HBL PBLHB2500005. The other is 24 short on AH-TMB-0019-BLK, expected 576 and received 552, on container TGHU7372239.
- **Supplier price changes:** Ceramics +3% from 1 Mar, Stainless +4% from 1 May, Textile +5% from 15 Aug, Electric −2% from 1 Jul.
- **Closures and logistics:** the Chinese New Year and National Day closures, sample couriers (AWB numbers), and deposit and balance payment amounts.
- **Defect lists** in the inspection reports.
- **Broker brokerage invoices** and last-free-day dates.
- **Voice messages**, which the manager asked the supplier to retype.
